name: Materialized View Refresh Strategies
tagline: Precomputing expensive joins and aggregations on disk for millisecond reads, trading bounded staleness for query speed.
purpose: Compare full, concurrent diff-merge, and incremental CDC/IVM materialized view refresh strategies and prevent AccessExclusiveLock outages.

spark.summary: Materialized view refresh precomputes and updates expensive joins or aggregations on disk so analytical queries read in milliseconds, trading bounded staleness and write/refresh overhead for read speed.
spark.keyTakeaway: Choose full concurrent refresh for simple batch dashboards, and incremental or CDC-driven refresh when tables exceed tens of millions of rows or require sub-minute freshness.

**Core Mechanics:** Unlike a standard SQL `VIEW` (which re-executes the query on every read), a **materialized view (MV)** persists the precomputed result set on disk and indexes it.

learningJourney.title: What is a Materialized View Refresh Strategy
learningJourney.explanation:
Unlike a standard SQL `VIEW` (which re-executes the query on every read), a **materialized view (MV)** persists the precomputed result set on disk and indexes it.

Its **refresh strategy** determines how base-table mutations propagate to the MV: **full recomputation** (`REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW`), **non-blocking concurrent diff-merge** (`CONCURRENTLY`), or **Incremental View Maintenance (IVM)** / CDC stream deltas.

sectionDiagram.title: CDC / WAL Delta Stream Feeding Incremental Materialized View

cards.label: 1. O(N) -> O(delta)
cards.detail: Instead of rescanning 500M rows every 5 minutes, IVM/CDC applies only changed keys.

cards.label: 2. Non-Blocking Reads
cards.detail: Postgres CONCURRENTLY or atomic table-swap keeps SELECT queries serving during refresh.

cards.label: 3. Bounded Staleness
cards.detail: APIs explicitly accept 5s–1h lag in exchange for predictable millisecond latency.

sectionDiagram.summary: Precomputing joins shifts O(N) scan cost from read time to an asynchronous refresh pipeline.

learningJourney.title: Why AccessExclusiveLock and Refresh Overlap cause outages
learningJourney.explanation:
Joining 500M-row fact tables on every dashboard load saturates disk I/O and blows past 200 ms API budgets. Yet naive MV refreshes cause two severe production incidents:
- **AccessExclusiveLock Read Outage**: running `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW` *without* `CONCURRENTLY` in PostgreSQL blocks all `SELECT` queries for minutes, piling up API threads.
- **Refresh Overlap Spiral**: as data grows, a 5-minute cron job takes 7 minutes; overlapping runs contend on locks and peg DB CPU at 100%.

ideas.title: Advisory Lock Overlap Guard
ideas.description: Wrap scheduled refreshes in `pg_try_advisory_lock(key)` so overlapping runs skip cleanly instead of piling up, and alert when duration > 70% of interval.

ideas.title: Unique Index Prerequisite
ideas.description: PostgreSQL `CONCURRENTLY` requires at least one `UNIQUE` index on the MV to compute the row-level diff.

learningJourney.title: Where Materialized Views excel (and where they do not)
learningJourney.explanation: Match MVs to repeated aggregations with predictable filter dimensions.

benefits: Repeated multi-table JOIN + GROUP BY queries drop from seconds to <20 ms.
costs: Bounded staleness (5 s to 1 h) and extra disk/WAL write amplification.

benefits: Query base OLTP tables directly for live bank balances or inventory deductions.
costs: MVs lag behind committed transactions unless maintained synchronously.

benefits: Use columnar engines (ClickHouse/DuckDB) when users filter on arbitrary unindexed columns.
costs: Unindexed MV scans are just as slow as base tables.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: Safe Concurrent Refresh with Advisory Lock Guard
learningJourney.explanation: Always pair a `UNIQUE` index with `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY`, and guard cron execution with `pg_try_advisory_lock`.
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Full Concurrent vs. Incremental IVM/CDC vs. Table Swap
learningJourney.explanation: Compare refresh mechanisms by table size, SQL expressiveness, and lock profile.

benefits: Supports arbitrary SQL (window functions, PERCENTILE); non-blocking SELECTs.
costs: O(N) compute per refresh; 2x–3x slower than exclusive refresh due to diff-merge WAL.

benefits: O(delta) updates in seconds regardless of total table size.
costs: Restricted SQL subset (e.g., complex outer joins or non-monotonic percentiles need care).

benefits: Zero diff overhead; fast bulk build into a staging table.
costs: Brief metadata lock on rename; must rebuild indexes on each swap.

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: Tiered Analytical Serving: Postgres MV -> ClickHouse/CDC
learningJourney.explanation: Teams start with PostgreSQL `CONCURRENTLY` for tables under ~50M rows, then graduate to **Debezium CDC -> ClickHouse Materialized Views** (using `SummingMergeTree` or `AggregatingMergeTree`) when base tables reach hundreds of millions of rows and dashboards demand <5-second freshness.

knowledgeCheck.question: What happens in PostgreSQL if you run REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW without CONCURRENTLY on a production dashboard view?

options.text: It updates only the rows that changed since the last refresh
options.feedback: Standard REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW always recomputes the entire view.

options.text: It acquires an AccessExclusiveLock, blocking all concurrent SELECT queries until the full refresh completes
options.feedback: Correct: always create a UNIQUE index and pass CONCURRENTLY in production to keep reads non-blocking.

options.text: It automatically drops all indexes on the view
options.feedback: Indexes remain, but readers are blocked for the duration of the refresh.
